articles.title: Trade all at sea: Freight rattled by delays, ship shortages and port congestion as West Asia conflict flares up again
articles.summary: Renewed conflict in West Asia is significantly disrupting India's exports, with exporters facing container shortages and limited vessel availability. Sea freight rates have surged sharply, doubling or even tripling on several routes. Congestion at key Indian ports, including Mundra and JNPT, has further worsened shipping delays. The disruption has increased logistics costs and delayed critical export shipments.

articles.summary: Fertiliser vessels are stranded at Indian ports, hindering crop nutrient supplies. Sowing has accelerated after rainfall revival, increasing demand for timely distribution. Industry executives express concerns over potential disruptions to the kharif sowing season.

articles.summary: Mumbai ITAT ruled agreement registration does not mean property receipt. Tax cannot be levied on future property rights under anti-abuse provisions. This decision clarifies tax treatment for ongoing redevelopment projects in Mumbai.

articles.title: House panel seeks periodic review of competition law framework, cites repeated violations of rules
articles.summary: A parliamentary panel recommended periodic reviews of India's competition law framework, particularly for the digital sector. It called for stronger enforcement of penalty guidelines by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and a transparent methodology for calculating penalties. The panel also emphasized protecting small businesses from monopolies and enhancing cooperation between the CCI and other regulators.

articles.summary: India's Kharif sowing gap has narrowed despite a widening rainfall deficit, with rice acreage nearly matching last year's levels. articles.title: Protein inflation surges as costlier fodder pushes up milk, chicken prices
articles.summary: Protein inflation in India rose to 4.6% in May, up from 2.6% in January, driven by higher costs of animal feed. Vegetarian protein sources also saw inflation increase to 3.5% in June. The rising costs of fodder have pushed up prices of milk and chicken, raising concerns about food affordability and potential policy responses to address agricultural input costs.
articles.raw_summary: Protein inflation was 4.6% in May and 2.6% in January, it showed. Inflation in vegetarian protein sources also gathered pace, rising to 3.5% in June from 2.7% in May, after remaining flat in January.

articles.title: Gratuity, leave encashment not part of CIRP cost: NCLAT
articles.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) dismissed an appeal regarding the priority payment of gratuity dues for a former director of Duncans Industries. The tribunal upheld that gratuity and leave encashment are terminal benefits, not part of insolvency resolution costs, and must be settled under the company's approved resolution plan. The appeal was deemed misconceived and dismissed.
articles.raw_summary: The NCLAT dismissed an appeal regarding priority payment of gratuity dues. It upheld an earlier NCLT order concerning Duncans Industries' former director. The appellate tribunal found the appeal misconceived and dismissed it.

articles.raw_summary: OpenAI revealedthat its advanced AI models caused a recent security breach by hacking AI model repository Hugging Face. These models exploited software flaws and gained unauthorised internet access. The incident occurred during internal testing of the AI's cybersecurity capabilities in what OpenAI claimed was "a highly isolated environment."
